source_text: delira reverteris: et adhibito ex Apostolo testimonio , illud quod de Abrahae et Sarrae emortuis membris dixeras, confirmare conaris. Unde iam superius, quantum satis visum est, me disseruisse suffecerit. Quis autem Christianus ignoret, quod
pass_a_gloss: Delira reverteris: and adhibito from Apostolo testimonio, that that/which about/from Abrahae and Sarrae emortuis members dixeras, confirmare conaris. whence already superius, quantum enough visum is, me disseruisse suffecerit. who however Christian ignoret, that/which.
pass_b_english: But from this digression, into which the force of grief carried [me], [I return] to what I had begun.
He who made the first human being from dust forms everyone from seed.
[The] defense of natural sin is strangled in [these] snares.

choices.why: Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
